reader.requirement: At 1985 every size-dependent action on a SYNCHRONIZED item (justification, truncation, size error/overflow, STRING pointer overflow, reference-modification bounds, INSPECT/LENGTH extent) must use the item's size from its PICTURE, USAGE and SIGN clauses, never any alignment slack, for display, binary, edited, scaled and table-element items.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2023 (DialectLevel < 2023) refuses SYNCHRONIZED on a group item (Constructs.SyncOnGroup2023, COBOL0900) per §1985:VI.5.13.3 SR1; elementary SYNC takes the same path at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Dialect|Construct in DataBinder.SynchronizedClause.cs: only GateSynchronizedGroup. grep -rn Synchronized over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen and src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime: only RepositoryAttributeRenderer (metadata); no layout, width, offset, file-record or move code reads the flag, so no edition arm exists on the storage path. The item's size is the PicInfo width, which the SYNC flag never changes (DOC-A.1-195: no padding).

reader.notes: Because the implementation performs no alignment (DOC-A.1-195), the SYNCHRONIZED flag never alters an item's width or offset, so every size-dependent action reads the PICTURE/USAGE/SIGN size. Probes over binary, display, edited, scaled and table SYNC items all honour that size.

refuter.evidence: Probe sy5.cob (sy5-003) tried size-dependent actions the reader did not. On an unsigned 9(4) COMP SYNC item, MOVE 12345 truncated to 002345, and ADD 1 to 9999 raised SIZE ERROR (U4B=009999). A PIC X(5) JUSTIFIED RIGHT SYNC LEFT item gave [   AB] and [CDEFG]. An S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE SYNC RIGHT item gave [-234]. UNSTRING into a PIC X(3) SYNC item gave [HEL] with COUNT 05. A 9(5) COMP SYNC element of an OCCURS table truncated 999999 to 099999, and MULTIPLY raised SIZE ERROR. COMPUTE of FUNCTION LENGTH(G) gave 22 = 2+5+4+3+2x4, no slack, and GA(6:9) of the group moved to X(30) was [FG-234HEL]. At 85, FUNCTION LENGTH written directly as a DISPLAY operand is refused (COBOL0900, a 2002 form), so I used COMPUTE. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.13.4 GR5 (the text is in GR5).
